story.head: Crash the net vs. bombs away
paras: The Blackhawks have won three straight, while the Rangers (13-10-1) lost 5-1 to Buffalo on Wednesday. Going in, the Rangers are fourth in the Metropolitan (18th in the NHL) and the Hawks last in the Central (28th).

The Rangers are one of the league’s most physical teams (2nd) and let the point shots come and guard the net (2nd). As for the Blackhawks, they get their shots through better than almost anyone (2nd) and pick their shots (2nd lowest), but don’t block many shots (31st). Chicago has allowed 3.84 goals a game, the third most in the league. The Rangers get in close, but the Blackhawks mostly shoot from distance. Beyond that, good looks are likely to be hard to come by for the Blackhawks.

Adam Fox (2 G / 25 A / 27 P in 24 GP) leads the Rangers in scoring, and Alexis Lafrenière (10 G / 12 A / 22 P in 24 GP) has a team-high ten goals. For the Blackhawks, Roman Kantserov (15 G / 5 A / 20 P in 25 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Sam Rinzel (2 G / 16 A / 18 P in 24 GP) isn’t far behind, with nine points in his last five games.
Dylan Garand (7-8-1 / .909 SV% in 14 GS) is expected to start for the Rangers, and Drew Commesso (1-0-0 / .880 SV% in 1 GS) for Chicago.

The Rangers are newly without Pavel Dorofeyev, Oliver Bjorkstrand and Gabe Perreault, and have been without Igor Shesterkin since Oct 9. Dylan Garand is expected to start. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Mammoth and the Avalanche are missing more right now.
